# Intake Draft — Add parent field to concise format of wl show output (WL-0MW5M5GUF0051D4N)

## Problem statement

The concise format of `wl show` (`-F concise`) omits the parent relationship entirely: an item with a parent shows no indication of it, so a user must switch to `normal` or `full` format to see which parent item a work item belongs to. The `normal` and `full` formats both already render a conditional `Parent` row; the `concise` format should do the same.

## Users

- **Primary**: Developers and operators using `wl show -F concise` (and `wl list -F concise`, which reuses the same formatter) to inspect work items compactly.
  - User story: As a user viewing a work item in concise format, I want to see its parent ID so I can trace the item's position in the work hierarchy without switching format.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl show <id> -F concise` renders a `Parent` row in the metadata table when the item has a `parentId` set, displaying the parent's ID. The row sits after `Effort` and before `Assignee`, matching the `normal`/`full` row order.
2. When the item has no parent, no `Parent` row appears in concise output (the row is conditional on `parentId` being set).
3. The `Parent` row renders correctly in both plain-text and markdown/TTY rendering of the concise format.
4. `wl list -F concise` tree rendering reflects the same change without regressing tree output (it delegates to the same formatter).
5. A unit test asserts the `Parent` row appears in concise output when `parentId` is set and is absent when it is not; all existing tests pass with the change.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Users of `wl show -F concise` can now see an item's parent at a glance, instead of switching to normal/full output to trace the hierarchy.

## Constraints

- **No changes** to `summary`, `raw`, `--fields` projected output, `normal`, or `full` formats.
- The `Parent` row is conditional on `parentId` being truthy — never a placeholder row in concise mode.
- Preserve the existing concise row order; insert `Parent` after `Effort`, before `Assignee`, consistent with `normal`/`full`.

## Existing state

- `src/commands/helpers.ts` → `humanFormatWorkItem()`: both `full` and `normal` format blocks already include `if (item.parentId) metaRows.push(['Parent', item.parentId]);`.
- The `concise` block (in the same function) builds its metadata table with: `Status` (incl. Stage | Priority), `SortIndex`, `Risk`, `Effort`, then conditional `Assignee`, `Audit`, `Tags` — no `Parent` row.
- Concise format is used by `wl show -F concise` and reused by the tree renderer `displayItemTreeWithFormat(items, db, 'concise')` for `wl list -F concise`.

## Desired change

- Add `if (item.parentId) metaRows.push(['Parent', item.parentId]);` to the `concise` block of `humanFormatWorkItem()` in `src/commands/helpers.ts`, after the `Effort` row.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — Add the conditional `Parent` row to the concise block of `humanFormatWorkItem()`.
- `tests/cli/helpers-tree-rendering.test.ts` — Logically adjacent concise-format tests (Risk/Effort rows); candidate home for the new coverage.
- `tests/unit/human-audit-format.test.ts` — Snapshot tests of concise/normal/full; items have no `parentId`, so unaffected, but adjacent precedent.
- `tests/integration/wl-show-formatting.test.ts` — Formatting integration tests (mock item has `parentId: null`; unaffected).
- `CLI.md` — `-F concise` documented only by examples; verify no row-by-row description needs updating.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: the `if (item.parentId)` truthiness guard matches `normal`/`full` behaviour (an empty string is treated as "no parent").
- **Assumption**: snapshot tests in `tests/unit/human-audit-format.test.ts` and `tests/cli/human-show-list-audit-snapshots.test.ts` use items without a parent, so no snapshot churn is expected; verify on run.
- **Scope-creep guard**: `--fields` projected output and `-f summary` are explicitly out of scope (recorded in Constraints); if the producer later wants them, they should be linked work items, not scope creep here.
- **Risk (low)**: `wl list -F concise` tree output will now include a `Parent` row per item — intended, but tree-rendering tests should be checked (AC4).

## Related work

- `WL-0MS6MOXNQ005B9IC` — Metadata in work-item detail views should be presented as markdown table (completed): established the markdown metadata table in full/normal/concise and the `Parent` row in full/normal; this item closes the concise-format gap.
- `WL-0MP14VZP8008ETDV` — Add integration tests for wl show formatted vs plain output (TTY/non-TTY) (completed): test precedent for show formatting.
- `WL-0MP14VZZG009KHPR` — Docs: document --format flag and CLI markdown behaviour (completed): `-F`/format documentation precedent.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **WL-0MMNCOJ0V0IFM2SN** – Audit Read Path in Show Outputs (completed)
- **WL-0MM8LXZ0M04W2YUF** – Human-readable and JSON output formatting (completed)
- **WL-0MS6MOXNQ005B9IC** – Metadata in work-item detail views should be presented as markdown table (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `CLI.md` — matched: add, concise, field, format, output (+2 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: add, field, format, output, parent (+1 more)
- `DATA_SYNCING.md` — matched: add, field, format, output, parent (+1 more)


## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "When should the `Parent` row appear in `-F concise` output — (a) only when `parentId` is set (conditional, matching normal/full), or (b) always with a `—` placeholder like Risk/Effort?" — Answer (operator): "(a) — conditional". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Scope — (a) only the `-F concise` human format, or (b) also `--fields` projected output and/or `-F summary`?" — Answer (operator): "(a) — `-F concise` only". Source: interactive reply.

# Ship opens in own tab (WL-0MW6FIZYI0003QEU)

**Headline**: The Ship It shortcut (`S`) dispatches the dev→main release (`/skill:ship release`) into a pi pane that currently splits the **current tab**. Change it so the release runs in **its own tab labelled `Ship`** in the invoking workspace — created on first use, reused thereafter, focused on open, placed left of the extensions/Work Items tab — and reject a second Ship command while the first release is still active.

## Problem statement

When an operator presses `S` in the herdr worklist selection list and confirms with `ship` + Enter, the release pi pane opens by splitting the current pane/tab, scattering the release in whatever tab the operator happened to be in. Ship is already a distinct, guarded workflow (typed-confirmation dialog, ship guard, code-freeze marker), so its pane should live in a dedicated, recognisable `Ship` tab — and a second release must not be started while the first is still running.

## Users

- **Herdr operator running a dev→main release**:
  > "As an operator, when I press `S` and confirm `ship`, I want the release pi session to open in a tab titled **Ship** so I can find it immediately and keep the release runner separate from the selection list and other work-tabs."
- **Operator running repeated releases**:
  > "As an operator who ships several times a day, I want the Ship tab to be reused (one release per tab) and a second Ship command rejected while a release is still active, so I never accidentally start two releases or clutter the tab row."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ship dispatch opens in its own tab** — pressing `S` and confirming with `ship` + Enter dispatches `/skill:ship release` into a tab labelled exactly `Ship` in the invoking pane's current workspace (created on first use, reused thereafter) instead of splitting the current pane/tab. Verified via `herdr tab list --workspace <ws>` (`label == 'Ship'`) and the spawned pi pane's `tab_id` matching that tab.
2. **Second Ship while active is rejected** — while the first release is still active (its Ship pane is live), a second `S` → confirm does **not** dispatch: a blocked notice is shown (no dialog/confirm opens), mirroring the existing ship-guard behaviour. No second pi pane is spawned.
3. **Focus the Ship pane** — the release pi pane is focused/zoomed on open so the operator immediately sees the release run (the pane may still be focused without stealing list focus, consistent with `focus: true` shortcut behaviour).
4. **Fresh Ship tab placed left-of-extensions** — a newly created `Ship` tab is placed immediately left of the extensions/Work Items tab (`'left-of-extensions'`), matching interactive item-ID tab placement; a reused tab is never repositioned.
5. **Fail-open placement** — if the `Ship` tab cannot be resolved or created (CLI failure, no workspace, guard query failure), the dispatch falls back to the current-pane split exactly as today — the release is never blocked by tab provisioning.
6. **Testing/validation** — unit + TUI integration tests cover: the Ship pane lands in the `Ship` tab (anchor pane id forwarded to `send-to-pi.sh`); the rejected second-command path; focus forwarding; left-of-extensions placement of a fresh tab; and the fail-open fallback.
7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs-site or wiki entries (e.g. the ship-it dialog / placement docs).
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

Operators can now start a dev→main release from the worklist and watch it run in a dedicated, always-findable `Ship` tab — with a fresh tab placed beside the work items and a second release safely rejected while the first is still running.

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing interactive tab machinery (`getItemTabAnchor` / `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor`, `herdr tab create --workspace <id> --label <label> --no-focus`) — do not introduce a parallel tab-provisioning path.
- The typed ship confirmation dialog (WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY), ship guard (WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW) and code-freeze marker flow stay intact; this item changes only *where* the dispatch pane lands and adds the second-command rejection.
- Global release command: `/skill:ship release` carries **no work-item ID**, so today `interactiveItemId` is `undefined` and the interactive item-ID anchor path returns `null`. The `Ship` label must be substituted for the missing item ID on this path only.
- Focus is currently *not* passed for the ship dispatch (`--no-focus`); this item adds focus explicitly.
- No push to `main`; work is committed to `dev` per the push policy.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `S` → `/skill:ship release` (view `both`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `openShipItDialogGuarded`/`openShipItDialog`; on confirm, `executeResolvedCommand(SHIP_IT_COMMAND, state, opts.onCommand, frozen, model, opts.onDowntimeToggle, undefined, opts.onRefresh)`; `dispatchChordCommand` routes `/skill:ship` → `resolveAndRouteCommand` → `onCommand(command, model, ...)` (paneTitle = selected item's title, focus undefined).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `onCommand` agent route: `interactiveItemId = extractWorkItemId(command)` → `undefined` for ship → `resolveInteractiveItemAnchorAfterAdmission` returns `null` → `--anchor` omitted → `send-to-pi.sh` splits the current pane (current tab).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.interactive.ts` — `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor(cwd, workspaceId, itemId, ...)` wraps `getItemTabAnchor`; fails open to `null` (current-pane split) on any error; supports `'left-of-extensions'` placement.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` — `getItemTabAnchor` creates-or-reuses a tab whose label is the key.
- `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.ts` — `runShipGuard`/`formatBlockedNotice` gate ship entry on live panes carrying project work-item IDs (blocked-notice UI already exists to reuse for the second-command rejection).

## Desired change

1. In the interactive agent dispatch path (`index.ts` `onCommand`), when the resolved command is `SHIP_IT_COMMAND` (`/skill:ship release`), resolve the interactive tab anchor with the literal label **`Ship`** instead of the (missing) work-item ID — reusing `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor`/`getItemTabAnchor` so the tab is created on first use and reused thereafter. Forward the anchor's pane id to `send-to-pi.sh` via `--anchor`, producing a pi pane inside the `Ship` tab.
2. Use `'left-of-extensions'` placement for a freshly created `Ship` tab (a reused tab is never moved).
3. Pass `focus: true` on the ship dispatch so the release pane is focused/zoomed on open.
4. Extend the ship-entry gate so a second Ship command is rejected while the first release is active: the guard (or a lightweight check on the same `shipGuardQuery` pane data) treats a live pane in the `Ship` tab as blocking — show the existing blocked notice, never open the confirmation dialog.
5. Fail-open: any anchor resolution/creation failure keeps today's current-pane split.

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — the `onCommand` agent route: substitute the `Ship` label for the item-ID anchor lookup, forward `--anchor` + `--focus`.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.interactive.ts` — `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor` (reused; may need a label param or ship-specific caller).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — ship dialog dispatch (`openShipItDialog.*`, `executeResolvedCommand` call), second-command rejection gate wiring, `SHIP_IT_COMMAND` handling.
- `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.ts` — extend guard result to include a live `Ship`-tab pane as a blocking condition (rejection path).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` / `.herdr-cli.ts` — existing `getItemTabAnchor` / `createTabInWorkspace` reused unchanged.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `S` shortcut entry (unchanged unless focus/code_freeze policy changes).
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/ship-it-dialog-tui.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard-tui.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.interactive.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.test.ts`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Title/requirement wording**: the item title says "own pane" but the requirement (and operator's confirmation) is an own *tab* labelled `Ship`; the pane inside the tab is the pi session. Implementation should key on the tab, not a pane rename.
- **Second-command rejection signal**: "first release still active" is interpreted as *a live pi pane in the `Ship` tab* (from the same `shipGuardQuery` pane list). If pane-liveness cannot be determined (query failure), fail safe the same way the existing guard does (blocked notice) — never open a second release.
- **Scope creep**: embedding extra capacity work in this item is out of scope — record as linked work items if discovered (e.g. a "reuse completed Ship tab" toggle, per-workspace Ship tabs, pane renaming policy).
- **Assumption**: placement, focus and rejection apply to the interactive `S` shortcut dispatch path only; other `/skill:ship` invocations keep current behaviour unless the same code path is shared.

## Related work

- WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY — Ship It shortcut + typed confirmation dialog (parent requirement: dispatch path).
- WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW — code freeze on ship confirmation + ship guard semantics (extension point for the second-command rejection).
- WL-0MUKZGEQ2007FECS — Pi processes start in a work-item tab (the item-ID tab machinery this item reuses with a fixed `Ship` label).
- WL-0MVZ88G51004IYHW / WL-0MW5E5V20002T0KW — left-of-extensions tab placement (fresh-tab placement policy).
- WL-0MUDEGBGO00609RV — ship-guard pure module (guard extension point).

## Related work (automated report)

- **WL-0ML5YRMB11GQV4HR** – Slash Command Palette (completed)
- **WL-0MSG6ZI3D003VYZZ** – Fix resize-mode anchor resolution: herdr pane current rejects --json (completed)
- **WL-0MTR2HLLJ009PTPJ** – Wire pane spawn to use persisted dispatcher anchor (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `CLI.md`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
- `packages/herdr/README.md`

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Tab lifecycle — should a second Ship command reuse an existing 'Ship' tab, or always open a fresh tab?" — Answer (operator): "A second ship command while the first is still active should be rejected." — Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: one release at a time — the `Ship` tab is created on first use and reused, and a second Ship command while the first release is active is blocked (never a fresh tab, never a second pane in the same tab). Prior options offered/rejected: reuse the tab (preferred at the time) vs fresh tab each time (rejected — would allow concurrent releases).
- Q2: "Where should a freshly created 'Ship' tab be placed?" — Answer (operator): **A — left-of-extensions** (same placement as interactive item-ID tabs, WL-0MW5E5V20002T0KW). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Should the Ship pane take focus when it opens?" — Answer (operator): **B — focus the Ship pane** so the operator immediately sees the release run. Source: interactive reply. Note: current behaviour is `--no-focus`; this item changes it for the Ship dispatch only.
data.title: Ship opens in own pane

## Goal

As an operator running the downtime dispatcher, I want a persisted Dispatcher
workspace / per-prefix tab anchor that no longer exists (herdr restarted, workspace
closed) to be **detected and re-provisioned automatically**, so that dispatch
self-heals after a herdr restart instead of silently refusing every candidate with
`anchor-unavailable` — leaving a 51-item backlog (plenty at `intake_complete` /
`plan_complete`) undispatched for hours with no visible cause.

## Reported symptom (measured 2026-11-15, ContextHub)

Intake and plan items are selected and nominated on every check-in
(`WL-0MWFMKWZA005ZT4T`, `WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR`, …) but never dispatched. The claim is
taken, placement fails, the claim is rolled back.

`.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`, blocking `no-dispatch` reasons,
2026-11-13T23:33Z → 2026-11-15T00:56Z:

| reason | count |
|---|---|
| **anchor-unavailable** | **124** |
| capacity-saturated | 40 |
| slots-unavailable | 35 |
| idle-window-spent | 20 |
| wl-error | 3 |

The live tick loop at the time of filing was `idle-age-qualified` →
`anchor-unavailable` → check-in re-offers → repeat (e.g. 00:56:04Z, 00:56:08Z).

## Root cause 1 — the persisted Dispatcher workspace is never validated, so the fallback can never recover

`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-anchor.json`:

```json
{"paneId":"w6A:p1","workspaceId":"w6A"}
```

`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json` (written 2026-11-14T23:50Z):

```json
{"workspaceId":"w6A","byPrefix":{"WL":{"tabId":"w6A:t2","paneId":"w6A:p5"}, ...}}
```

Workspace **`w6A` no longer exists**. Live `herdr workspace list` at filing:
`w52, w8, w4F, w3G, w5M, w50, w5S, w57`.

Verified by driving the real modules:

```
herdr pane get w6A:p5   -> {"code":"pane_not_found"}
herdr tab get  w6A:t2   -> {"code":"tab_not_found"}
listTabsInWorkspace(root, 'w6A') -> null
```

The failure chain:

1. `getDispatcherTabAnchor` (`dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts`) step 2 checks the
   cached pane with `isPaneAlive` → `false` → correctly falls through to
   re-provision. **The dead pane IS detected.**
2. Step 1 `ensureDispatcherWorkspace(deps)` does **not** validate the cached
   workspace: `readDispatcherWorkspaceId()` returns `w6A` verbatim and it is
   returned as the target workspace. A dead pane id is therefore converted into a
   dead *workspace* id, which nothing checks.
3. Step 3 `resolvePrefixTab` → `listTabs(w6A)` → `null` → `{status:'unknown'}`.
4. `unknown` fails closed by design ("never guess, never duplicate") →
   `getDispatcherTabAnchor` returns `null`.
5. `resolveDispatchPlacement` (`downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts`) returns
   `{ok:false}`; the per-prefix resolver **deliberately never falls back** to the
   legacy `getDispatcherAnchor`. So `anchor-unavailable`, claim rolled back, and the
   next tick repeats it forever.

The two self-healing paths are mutually exclusive: the per-prefix resolver is the
one that is reachable and it cannot heal; `getDispatcherAnchor` (which *does*
self-heal — it checks pane liveness and re-provisions a fresh workspace) is
unreachable because the per-prefix resolver replaced it.

**Why nothing cleans it:** there is no reaper or TTL for either anchor file.
`persistPrefixTab` / `writeTabAnchors` / `writeAnchor` only ever write;
`readAnchor` / `readTabAnchors` validate the file *shape*, never that the referenced
workspace/tab/pane still exist. `WL-0MWFIZIAU007RBER` added pruning for the
*coordination* file, not for anchors. Every herdr restart therefore leaves a stale
workspace id that permanently wedges placement for every prefix.

## Root cause 2 — the primary placement path cannot match this project's workspace (contributing)

`resolveProjectWorkspace` matches on the plugin pane's `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` only.
The ContextHub "Work Items" pane reports
`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD=/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/herdr`, not the
worklog root, so:

```
resolveProjectWorkspace('/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub', deps, <same>) -> null
```

Other roots match (AH, RISE, TCE, SA), which is why their panes dispatch and
ContextHub's does not. Because the primary path returns `null`, ContextHub falls
through to the wedged fallback in Root cause 1 — hence the total starvation. Fixing
Root cause 1 restores dispatch, but panes land in the Dispatcher workspace's `WL`
tab rather than the ContextHub workspace until this mismatch is also addressed.

## Proposed fix

**A. Validate the persisted workspace (the actual unblock).**

- `ensureDispatcherWorkspace` validates the persisted `workspaceId` still exists
  before reuse (`listTabs(<ws>)` parsed result, or `herdr workspace list`) and, when
  it is gone, provisions a fresh Dispatcher workspace and rewrites
  `downtime-dispatch-anchor.json`.
- `getDispatcherTabAnchor` distinguishes **workspace missing** (recoverable →
  re-provision) from **herdr unreadable** (transient CLI error → fail closed, no
  duplicate workspace).
- Prune `byPrefix` entries that reference a dead workspace when rewriting the map,
  so stale ids cannot accumulate and mask later wedges.

**B. Diagnostics.** `anchor-unavailable` decision-log entries carry the detail
(missing workspace id vs unreadable CLI) so the next occurrence is diagnosable from
the log.

**C. Primary path.** Record the `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` mismatch as a diagnostic
decision entry, and document the operator remedy (start the plugin pane from the
worklog root). Whether to broaden the matching rule (ancestor/descendant match) is a
decision for plan time — a wrong-workspace match is worse than a fallback, so the
default is: do not change the matching rule in this item unless AC8 is satisfied
without ambiguity.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Stale workspace self-heals.** With `downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` and
   `downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json` pointing at a workspace that does not exist,
   `getDispatcherTabAnchor(cwd, deps, 'WL')` provisions a fresh Dispatcher workspace
   and returns a live anchor for a new tab — instead of `null`. Regression test
   reproduces today's exact state (`w6A` gone) against injected deps.
2. **Dead pane still heals.** The existing behaviour is preserved: a persisted
   prefix entry whose *pane* is dead (workspace alive) still re-resolves/re-creates
   the tab. Pinned by a test so AC1 does not regress the fast path.
3. **No duplicate workspaces.** A transient/unreadable herdr (`tab list` CLI error
   or unparseable output) still fails closed with `anchor-unavailable` and provisions
   nothing. Concurrent first-dispatchers (coordination lock + double-check) create at
   most one replacement workspace — test asserts `createWorkspace` is called once for
   two racing callers.
4. **Stale prefix entries pruned.** Rewriting the tab-anchor map drops `byPrefix`
   entries whose workspace id is the dead one; a test asserts the persisted file
   after recovery contains no `w6A`-style dead ids.
5. **End-to-end dispatch unblocks.** `resolveDispatchPlacement` returns `{ok:true}`
   in the reproduced stale-anchor state (test), and the occurrence no longer
   produces repeated `anchor-unavailable` decisions on consecutive ticks
   (orchestrator-level test with a stale anchor store).
6. **Diagnosable refusal.** When placement genuinely fails closed, the
   `anchor-unavailable` decision entry includes a machine-readable detail naming the
   failing boundary (persisted-workspace-missing vs herdr-unreadable), and a test
   asserts the field is present.
7. **Primary-path mismatch is visible.** A diagnostic is recorded when
   `resolveProjectWorkspace` fails to match a root whose plugin pane reports a
   different `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` (naming expected vs actual), and the failure is
   documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` with the operator remedy.
8. **Matching rule unchanged unless unambiguous.** `resolveProjectWorkspace`'s
   match semantics are unchanged in this item. If plan chooses to add
   ancestor/descendant matching it must be covered by an ambiguity test (two panes
   claiming the same root resolve deterministically: focused first, then lowest pane
   id).
9. **Docs.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` placement section states: persisted
   anchors are validated against live herdr state on every resolution; a vanished
   workspace is re-provisioned once; an unreadable herdr still fails closed; and no
   anchor file has a TTL — recovery is on-read validation, not a reaper.
10. **No spawn/latency regression.** The validation adds no `wl` spawn (it reuses
    already-issued herdr calls); `fetcher-spawn-cap` / split-guard suites stay green
    and the refresh budget is unchanged.
11. **Full suite green.**

## Immediate mitigation (not the fix)

For the live machine, dispatch is wedged **now**; deleting
`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` and
`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json` forces re-provisioning on the
next tick. Recorded so the operator can unblock before this item lands — the code
fix must make that manual step unnecessary.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts` — `ensureDispatcherWorkspace` (no workspace validation), `getDispatcherTabAnchor` (`unknown` → `null`), `getDispatcherAnchor` (the self-healing path that is currently unreachable).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.persistence.ts` — `readDispatcherWorkspaceId`, `readTabAnchors`, `persistPrefixTab`, `writeAnchor` (write-only; no pruning, no validation).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` — `resolveProjectWorkspace` (`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` only), `getItemTabAnchor`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` — `resolveDispatchPlacement` precedence and the `{ok:false}` / `anchor-unavailable` verdict.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.anchor-resolvers.ts` — `defaultDispatcherAnchorResolver` / `defaultDispatcherTabAnchorResolver` / `defaultProjectWorkspaceResolver` (the deps that roll up the failures).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` — existing anchor tests (stale-pane cases) to extend with stale-workspace cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.test.ts` (or nearest placement suite) — `resolveDispatchPlacement` precedence tests.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — placement / anchor documentation.

## Non-goals

- Adding a TTL or background reaper for anchor files — recovery is on-read validation.
- Changing the per-prefix-does-not-fall-back-to-legacy-anchor rule.
- Re-provisioning on a transient herdr read failure (that must stay fail-closed).
- Broadening `resolveProjectWorkspace` matching semantics without the AC8 ambiguity
  guarantee.
- Changing `send-to-pi.sh` / pane spawn behaviour, or the project-workspace tab
  placement policy for roots that do match.

## Decisions already taken

- **Validation over reaping.** A missing workspace is recovered on read, not by an
  age-based reaper: an anchor is stale because the thing it points at is gone, not
  because it is old.
- **Missing ≠ unreadable.** Only a positively-observed missing workspace triggers
  provisioning; an unreadable herdr keeps today's fail-closed behaviour.
- **One recovery mechanism.** Reuse `getDispatcherAnchor`'s existing
  provision-under-lock + double-check path rather than a second implementation.

## Related

- `WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC` — per-prefix Dispatcher tabs (introduced the resolver that
  replaced the legacy anchor and created this unreachable-healer situation).
- `WL-0MUR5FUWD00024XN` — placement precedence (project workspace → per-prefix tab
  → legacy anchor) docs/tests this item extends.
- `WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG` — Dispatcher anchor origin (C0).
- `WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU` — Dispatcher placeholder root-pane adoption (same file
  family).
- `WL-0MWFIZIAU007RBER` — coordination-file pruning precedent (a reaper for the
  coordination file; deliberately **not** mirrored for anchors).
- `WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9` — precedent: an un-timed failure path silently wedging the
  dispatch task.
- `WL-0MWFMKWZA005ZT4T`, `WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR` — the prep-tier items repeatedly
  nominated and never dispatched in the reported window.

## Impact

A herdr restart can no longer silently wedge the downtime dispatcher: persisted
placement anchors self-heal on the next tick, so the backlog keeps moving and an
operator no longer has to delete anchor files to get work dispatched.
data.title: Downtime dispatcher: a persisted Dispatcher anchor pointing at a dead herdr workspace wedges placement forever (anchor-unavailable) — validate on read and re-provision

data.description:
discovered-from:WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH

## Goal

As an operator relying on the downtime dispatcher, I want the hydrator to treat a
live dispatch pane as evidence the item is being worked on **wherever that pane
lives**, so a claim is never released seconds after its pane spawns — otherwise the
item falls back into the dispatch pool while an agent is still working it (churn,
and a duplicate-dispatch window).

## Reported symptom (measured 2026-11-15, ContextHub)

Five seconds after a downtime dispatch spawned a working pane, the hydrator
released the dispatch claim under it:

```
01:11:14.792Z  downtime worker  dispatched WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR (kind: plan) -> pane w6B:p3
01:11:15.429Z  herdr-downtime  Auto-dispatched … running /skill:plan WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR
01:11:19.468Z  herdr-hydrator  released because no matching pane; previous assignee: dispatcher
```

At the moment of release the pane was demonstrably alive:

```
herdr pane list --workspace w6B
  w6B:p3  w6B:t2  'Downtime triggered plan finish moves … - WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR'  agent_status: working
```

and the work item was back to `status=open`, `assignee:""` (dispatchable) while that
agent kept running.

The same release had already hit this item's earlier intake dispatch:

```
00:50:37.481Z  dispatched WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR (kind: intake)
00:50:06.219Z  herdr-hydrator  released because no matching pane; previous assignee: dispatcher
```

That is the mechanism behind the repeated re-nomination of prep items: dispatch →
claim → hydrator release → item dispatchable again → dispatch, indefinitely.

## Root cause 1 — pane evidence is scoped to the plugin's own workspace, but fallback placement puts panes in the Dispatcher workspace

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:5733` and `packages/herdr/src/index.ts:1758-1760`
  build the hydrator with `workspaceId: process.env.HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` — the
  **plugin pane's** workspace (ContextHub: `w5M`).
- `createProductionHydratorDeps().listActivePanes(workspaceId)` runs
  `herdr pane list --workspace w5M`, so only the plugin's own panes are returned.
- `collectPaneWorkItemIds(panes, workspaceId)` then filters any pane whose
  `workspace_id` differs (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts:409-431`).
- `runHydrationOnce` derives `const hasActivePane = paneIds.has(item.id)`
  (`hydrator.ts:~897`); false ⇒ `decideDemotion` releases the claim.

Downtime placements that cannot use the project-workspace path are deliberately
placed in the **Dispatcher** workspace's per-prefix tab
(`downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` precedence: project workspace + item tab →
per-prefix Dispatcher tab → legacy Dispatcher anchor). Today that is *every*
ContextHub dispatch, because the plugin pane reports
`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD=/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/herdr`, so
`resolveProjectWorkspace` returns `null` and the fallback is used. The resulting
pane (`w6B:p3`) is in a different workspace from the plugin (`w5M`) and is therefore
invisible to the hydrator: **`hasActivePane` is deterministically false, not
racily false.**

The same trap applies to any future root whose primary placement path fails, so this
is not ContextHub-specific.

## Root cause 2 — the claim-holder backstop does not cover prep/audit dispatches

The "busy = pane OR live claim holder" protection (`WL-0MVWDB3IG004NRIU`,
`claim-lock.ts`) is the intended second signal. But it reads
`<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock`, which is taken by the *implement* work-item lock,
not by `/skill:intake`, `/skill:plan` or audit runs — verified: there is no
`child-WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR.lock` while its plan pane was live. So for the prep tier
pane visibility is the **only** signal, and that signal is workspace-scoped
(Root cause 1). The release comment says `released because no matching pane` rather
than `… and claim holder dead`, confirming no live holder was seen.

## Root cause 3 (residual) — no grace window between spawn and pane visibility

Even within one workspace, a hydrator tick that lands between `send-to-pi.sh`
spawning a pane and the pane title/marker becoming readable sees no pane for a
just-claimed item. Nothing bounds that window: `decideDemotion` consults only
`hasActivePane`, `blocked` and `held`.

## Proposed fix

**A. Cross-workspace pane evidence (the actual fix).**
Derive the demotion signal from a workspace-agnostic pane read (or from the union of
the plugin workspace and the Dispatcher workspace(s) in use), while keeping the
*display* marker scoped to the plugin workspace as today. Two different questions —
"is this item being worked on?" (anywhere) vs "does this item have a pane in my
workspace?" (display) — must not share one filter.

**B. Fail-open when the wider read is unavailable.** If the cross-workspace pane
list cannot be read, do not release (fail-open to keeping the claim), matching the
existing fail-open rule for an unavailable dep lookup.

**C. Bound the spawn→visible window.** Do not release an item whose dispatch marker
/ claim is younger than a documented grace window (reuse the existing marker
recency concept rather than a new timestamp field if one already exists).

**D. Keep the claim-holder backstop honest.** Either the dispatcher records a claim
holder for prep/audit spawns, or the hydrator's decision documents that pane
evidence is the only signal for those tiers — with a test pinning the chosen
contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Cross-workspace pane prevents release.** With a pane titled
   `Downtime triggered plan … - WL-XXXX` alive in the **Dispatcher** workspace and
   the item `in-progress` with `assignee: dispatcher`, `runHydrationOnce` makes **no**
   release and writes no `released because no matching pane` comment. Regression test
   reproduces today's exact state (plugin workspace `w5M`, pane in `w6B`).
2. **Display marker scope unchanged.** The selection-list "working" marker
   (`applyActivePaneMarkers` / `markItemsActiveByPane`) still reflects only panes in
   the plugin's own workspace — a cross-workspace pane must not light up the marker.
   Pinned by a test so AC1 does not silently widen the display path
   (`WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ` intent preserved).
3. **Genuine absence still releases.** An `in-progress` item with no pane in **any**
   workspace and no live claim holder is still released, with today's comment text.
   Pinned by a test (no over-correction into never releasing).
4. **Fail-open on an unreadable wider read.** When the cross-workspace pane read
   fails/returns null, the hydrator does not release (keeps the claim) and does not
   spam release comments. Pinned by a test.
5. **Grace window bounded.** An item claimed within the configured grace window is
   never released even if no pane is visible yet; after the window, today's rule
   applies. Test covers both sides of the boundary with an injected clock.
6. **No release storm / no duplicate dispatch.** After a dispatch, while its pane is
   live, the item is not returned to the dispatchable pool: a test asserts that a
   dispatched prep item is not re-offered/nominated on subsequent cycles while its
   pane exists (today it is re-offered every cycle).
7. **Prep-tier signal contract recorded.** The chosen contract for prep/audit tiers
   (Root cause 2: pane evidence only, or a recorded claim holder) is documented in
   the hydrator header comment and covered by a test for whichever option is chosen.
8. **Diagnostics.** A release records the evidence that justified it (panes seen,
   workspaces scanned, age of the claim) so a future mis-release is diagnosable from
   the comment/log without reading pane state by hand.
9. **Docs.** `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` (or the hydrator section of
   `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`) states: demotion evidence is cross-workspace;
   display markers stay workspace-scoped; the grace window and its default.
10. **No latency regression.** The wider pane read reuses the existing pane-list
    call where possible (no new per-item spawn); hydrator step budgets
    (`HYDRATOR_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS`) and the responsiveness suite stay green.
11. **Full suite green.**

## Immediate mitigation (not the fix)

The dispatcher re-claiming the item after each release is what keeps work moving
today, so it is self-limiting but churny — and it leaves a duplicate-dispatch window
if the item is re-selected before the running pane finishes. No manual action is
required; this is recorded so the operator knows today's behaviour is a workaround,
not correct behaviour.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — `collectPaneWorkItemIds` (workspace filter),
  `runHydrationOnce` (`hasActivePane`), `decideDemotion`, `createHydratorRunner`,
  `createProductionHydratorDeps` (`listActivePanes` → `pane list --workspace`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — hydrator wiring with
  `process.env.HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` (~line 5733); `applyActivePaneMarkers` display use
  (~line 1994 in `index.ts` parallels it).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `hydratorDeps` / `hydratorWorkspaceId` (~1758-1760).
- `packages/herdr/src/claim-lock.ts` — claim-holder heldness probe (the backstop that
  does not apply to prep tiers).
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — title builders and
  `truncatePaneTitlePreservingSuffix` (the id-as-suffix contract the scan relies on).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` — why fallback panes land
  in the Dispatcher workspace (the trigger condition).
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts`, `hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts` — test homes.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — docs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the placement precedence (project workspace → per-prefix tab → legacy
  anchor). Panes landing in the Dispatcher workspace is intended behaviour.
- Changing how `pane-title.ts` builds or truncates titles.
- Making display markers cross-workspace (explicitly excluded by AC2).
- Removing the demotion mechanism: releasing genuinely pane-less claims stays.
- Retroactively re-claiming items that were released during this bug's lifetime.

## Decisions already taken

- **Keep the claim on ambiguity.** Every ambiguous read (unreadable pane list,
  pane-list inside the grace window) keeps the claim. A stuck claim is recoverable;
  a released claim under a live agent is not.
- **One filter per question.** Demotion evidence is workspace-agnostic; display is
  workspace-scoped. They must not share a helper call with a shared workspace
  argument.

## Related

- `WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH` — the Dispatcher-anchor wedge that forces ContextHub onto the
  fallback placement path (this bug's trigger condition). Discovered-from that item.
- `WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ` — pane-title-based active matching and the
  truncate-preserving-suffix contract; its `workspaceId` scoping is the code under
  change (the display half must be preserved).
- `WL-0MVWDB3IG004NRIU` — "busy = pane OR live claim holder" cycle wiring (the
  backstop that does not cover prep tiers).
- `WL-0MVW9UQQ6004KSXY` — hydrator demoting pane-less driven sessions (the previous
  hydrator over-release bug; this item is its cross-workspace sibling).
- `WL-0MVWDB7F2003SORI` / `WL-0MVWDBF71005EJM0` — claim release naming the previous
  holder (the comment format relied on by AC8).
- `WL-0MUR5FUWD00024XN` — placement precedence that sends fallback dispatches to the
  Dispatcher workspace.

## Impact

An agent's claim is no longer released seconds after its pane spawns, so operators
stop seeing items bounce back into the dispatch list while an agent is still working
them — and the duplicate-dispatch window that churn created is closed.
data.title: Hydrator releases a live dispatch claim seconds after spawn: demotion pane evidence is workspace-scoped, so fallback-placed panes in the Dispatcher workspace are invisible
